title: Two Flags on One Cart

opening.dialogue: A life is a sending, and the last rai sends up its smell of wet clay and diesel. Kwang stands at the edge of the unbuilt field with a phone mount clamped to a fence post, a woman running at five percent, filming a mortar that has not yet been sold.
The light is better here than at the cart. Pa Yong's mortar on the last rai — that's the whole campaign in one frame.
The granite mortar sits on a plastic stool where the field meets the soi. Mint's laminated menu is taped to its side. Nobody has pounded anything in it since the order came in.

turns.speaker: char_kwang
stage_directions: She tilts the phone mount toward the mortar and taps the screen with one finger.
turns.dialogue: I told my team this was a beach shoot. Sand, salt, a mortar — they believed me. Nobody checks a background twice when the light is good.

turns.speaker: char_kwang
stage_directions: She lifts the laundry basket off the stool and sets it on the grass, then brushes a leaf from the rim.
turns.dialogue: Pa Yong thinks I'm stealing something. I'm not. The mortar stays hers. I just need it to look like it belongs to everyone.

turns.speaker: char_kwang
stage_directions: She points the phone mount at a water buffalo grazing at the field's far edge, then pans back to the mortar.
turns.dialogue: That buffalo has been eating since I got here. No stopping, no posing. If I could sell that kind of patience, I'd be finished by noon.

turns.speaker: char_kwang
stage_directions: She checks the phone mount's clamp, then glances at the orange queue vest folded on the basket.
turns.dialogue: My mother thinks I work in a bank. If she saw me photographing a mortar for a brand, she'd ask why I can't just come home and pound som tam like a normal daughter.

turns.speaker: char_kwang
stage_directions: She turns the phone mount toward Lek and holds it steady, waiting.
turns.dialogue: You read documents for people. You know what a thing means before it's said. Tell me — does this mortar look like a memory or a product?

turns.speaker: char_kwang
stage_directions: She taps the laminated menu taped to the mortar's side, then looks at Lek.
turns.dialogue: Mint calls it 'Heritage Fusion.' Pa Yong calls it nothing. I need a name that sells without lying. What would you call it?

turns.speaker: char_kwang
stage_directions: She opens the laundry basket and takes out a small plastic container of som tam, holding it toward Lek.
turns.dialogue: Mint's new recipe. I'm supposed to taste it before I photograph it. I'll try it if you will — one bite each, and then we decide.

turns.speaker: char_kwang
stage_directions: She lowers the phone mount and sets it on the stool beside the mortar.
turns.dialogue: Pa Yong and I used to talk every week. Now she sends the order through Mint. We don't stay in touch — we just send things and hope they arrive.

kwang_turn_1.speaker: char_kwang
kwang_turn_1.line: She frames the mortar against the field and the buffalo, and the shot looks like a postcard from a place that no longer exists.

kwang_turn_2.speaker: char_kwang
kwang_turn_2.line: She folds the basket's rim and sets it beside the mortar. The two objects sit together like a before and after.

kwang_turn_3.speaker: char_kwang
kwang_turn_3.line: The buffalo keeps eating. Kwang keeps filming. Neither of them stops for the other.

kwang_turn_4.speaker: char_kwang
kwang_turn_4.line: She smooths the orange vest flat on the basket and says nothing about her mother for a long moment.

kwang_turn_5.speaker: char_kwang
kwang_turn_5.line: She waits. The phone mount trembles slightly in her hand, the way a hand does when it has been holding a question too long.

kwang_turn_6.speaker: char_kwang
kwang_turn_6.line: She peels back the tape on the menu and reads Mint's handwriting aloud, then laughs once, without humor.

kwang_turn_7.speaker: char_kwang
kwang_turn_7.line: She takes a bite, chews, and sets the container down. 'It's good,' she says. 'That's the problem.'
kwang_turn_7.bubble: Kwang has tasted Mint's fusion som tam

kwang_turn_8.speaker: char_kwang
kwang_turn_8.line: She picks up the phone mount and turns it off. The screen goes dark; the mortar sits in the last daylight like something waiting to be claimed.

finale.dialogue: She hands Lek the funeral gimbal — the one from the wat, still scuffed from Novice Toy's livestream. 'For your shop,' she says. 'You read things for people. Maybe you can read this.'

The mortar stays on the last rai. The buffalo keeps eating. Kwang walks back toward the tower with her phone dark in her hand, a woman running at five percent, and the field sends up its smell of clay and diesel into the night.

obj_stamp_keys.name: the stamp-drawer keys
obj_stamp_keys.description: Two brass keys on a wire ring, worn smooth at the bow, one stamped with a number Lek has never needed to read.

obj_biscuit_tin.name: the biscuit tin of ledgers
obj_biscuit_tin.description: A Khun Sanga's biscuit tin, lid dented at one corner, holding three vendors' books in rubber-banded stacks and a smell of old paper and sweet crumbs.

obj_word_notebook.name: the word notebook
obj_word_notebook.description: A pocket notebook with a cracked spine, half-filled with other people's words in Lek's small hand, no page numbered.

obj_coin_stack.name: the stack of ten-baht coins
obj_coin_stack.description: Ten coins stacked on the stool, counted twice, the top one warm from someone's pocket.

obj_gimbal.name: the funeral gimbal
obj_gimbal.description: A handheld gimbal with a scuffed grip and a wat sticker half-peeled from its arm, used for Novice Toy's livestream and now for whatever comes next.

obj_mortar.name: the granite mortar
obj_mortar.description: A heavy granite mortar, rim chipped at one edge, with a laminated menu taped to its side and a faint smell of lime and fish sauce in the stone.

obj_laundry_basket.name: the laundry basket
obj_laundry_basket.description: A plastic laundry basket with one cracked rib, holding a folded orange vest and a small container of som tam wrapped in a plastic bag.

obj_phone_mount.name: the phone mount
obj_phone_mount.description: A clamp-style phone mount with a rubber jaw and a tripod thread, the clamp face scratched from fence posts and cart edges.

obj_vest_orange.name: the orange queue vest
obj_vest_orange.description: A high-visibility orange vest, folded small, the reflective strips gone gray at the seams from too many washes.

outcomeRules.speaker: char_kwang
outcomeRules.line: She turns the keys over in her palm and reads the stamped number. 'You keep other people's drawers. So you know what it costs to open one that isn't yours.'
outcomeRules.bubble: Kwang has seen the stamp-drawer keys

outcomeRules.speaker: char_kwang
outcomeRules.line: She opens the tin and reads a page of Pa Yong's ledger upside down, correctly. 'Three vendors' books in one tin. That's the whole soi in a biscuit box.'
outcomeRules.bubble: Kwang has read the biscuit tin's ledgers

outcomeRules.speaker: char_kwang
outcomeRules.line: She flips through the notebook and stops at a page where Lek has written 'Heritage Fusion' in the margin. 'You already named it,' she says. 'You just didn't send it.' She presses the gimbal into his hands.

char_kwang: She glances at the {item} and shakes her head, once, as if the light had changed. 'Not that. Not yet.'
She sets the {item} down on the stool between them. 'Pa Yong's mortar is the whole question. Everything else is after the question.'
She taps the {item} against her palm and looks at the mortar. 'Open something of yours first. Then ask me about mine.'
narrator: The {item} goes back into the night with nothing settled. The buffalo keeps eating; the field keeps sending up its smell.
Nothing comes of the {item} yet. Kwang watches the mortar the way a clerk watches a clock.
Kwang's gaze flicks from the {item} to the keys in Lek's pocket and back — a drawer mapped, a toll implied.
